questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

I was sitting at home doing nothing when I __had heard__ that song again.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3 i.e. heard.**

 
• **'Had heard'** is in the past perfect tense. Past perfect tense is used when we are talking about an action that took place before another past action. In the given sentence, there is no such mention.
 
• The sentence uses **'was'** which indicates that it in the past tense and we need to use the past tense form of the verb i.e. heard.

 

So, **'heard'** makes the sentence grammatically correct.

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.**

**A.** They also visit ailing friends and relatives or attend to personal matters even during office hours.

**B. **Once in office, they receive friends and relatives who call them any time without prior appointment.

**C.** We can frequently find a large number of people sitting here and there and doing nothing.

**D.** Even those who are employed often come late to office and leave early unless they are forced to be punctual.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1 i.e. CDBA.**

__
 
• **C** is the sentence that **establishes the subject matter**. Hence, it'll be the **first sentence **after rearrangement.
 
• D starts with 'even those' which refers to people mentioned in C. Hence, **D** follows C.
 
• Sentence **B** is the logical successor of D as it talks about people in the office mentioned in D.
 
• Last comes **A **as it uses 'also' and elaborates sentence B.

**Sentences after rearrangement-**__

*We can frequently find a large number of people sitting here and there and doing nothing. Even those who are employed often come late to office and leave early unless they are forced to be punctual. Once in office, they receive friends and relatives who call them any time without prior appointment. They also visit ailing friends and relatives or attend to personal matters even during office hours.*

questions.question:
**Select the word which means the same as the group of words given.**

Having something more than required
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **Surplus**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Surplus"** means having more than what is needed or used; an excess amount. (अधिशेष)

 
 
• **Example:** The farmer had a surplus of crops this year, more than he could sell.
 
 
 
• **"Surplus"** refers specifically to having an extra quantity of something that is more than what is required. (अधिशेष)
 
 
• **Example:** The company decided to use the surplus funds to invest in new technology.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Surplus**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Surroundings** (परिवेश): The environment or area around a particular place.

 
 
• **Example:** She felt safe in the familiar surroundings of her hometown.
 
 
 
• **Surcharge** (अधिभार): An additional charge or payment.
 
 
• **Example:** The hotel added a surcharge for the extra services we requested.
 
 
 
• **Surrogate** (प्रतिनिधि): A substitute, especially a person deputizing for another in a specific role or office.
 
 
• **Example:** She acted as a surrogate during her colleague's maternity leave.

questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

We must get this post send as soon as possible
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2.**

 
• **'Send'** is the base form of the verb and is mostly used in the present tense to give an order to someone. It is used in the active voice and an action that is occurring in the present.
 
• Eg- **Send** her gifts.
 
• '**Sent'** is the past participle form of the verb and is used in the passive voice. It is also used to indicate an action that has occurred in the past.
 
• Eg- The letter has been **sent.**
 
• The given sentence indicates the action of sending must be done. It is not being done in the present. So, we must use **'sent'** instead of **'send'** to make the sentence correct.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No improvement'.**

One evening, when father was coming home from work, I __played__ in the front garden.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1 i.e. was playing.**

 
• The speaker is talking about something that occurred in the past while another action was happening. The other action was **'father was coming home'** and at the same time the speaker was playing.
 
• Here we need to use the past continuous tense for something that was happening in the past.
 
• **'Played'** is used in the simple past tense.
 
• Eg- *I played football yesterday.*

We will use **'was playing'** instead of **'played**' to make the sentence correct.
